key_insight: LLM-based radiology metrics can detect true clinical errors well, but many also over-penalize harmless wording changes, so the key challenge is balancing discrimination and robustness.
clinical_relevance: A better metric can judge generated radiology reports more reliably, helping reduce clinically important mistakes without unfairly rejecting acceptable report variations.
method: Tested 8 LLM evaluators on the ReEvalMed benchmark in one-pass and two-pass settings
Measuring two dimensions: Discrimination for catching true errors and Robustness for tolerating benign rephrasings
Trained lightweight interpretable metrics on 4k synthesized report pairs using Qwen3-8B and MedGemma-4B
evidence_signal: The trained metric outperformed 32B-scale medical LLM evaluators and stayed competitive with proprietary models, while two-pass inference did not consistently improve overall performance.
watch_item: Even strong metrics may still over-penalize harmless variations, so deployment should be checked for the desired discrimination-robustness balance before use.
paper_title: Beyond Scalar Scores: Exploring LLM-based Metrics for Clinical Significance Evaluation in Radiology Reports
